bmtx.name: BMT-X
bmtx.what: Boosting with multiple testing (Kapetanios, Sarafidis & Ventouri), the method from my thesis. One model per hour, with weather, holidays and gas.

learx.name: LEAR-X
learx.what: Lasso on the last two years of prices and inputs, one model per hour. The standard benchmark in price forecasting papers.

xgbx.name: XGBoost-X
xgbx.what: Gradient-boosted trees on the same inputs as LEAR-X.

r_net.name: R network
r_net.what: A small network written in base R: two layers (192 and 96), dropout, Huber loss. Three seeds averaged, refit every day.

torch_plain.name: PyTorch network
torch_plain.what: Two layers (256 and 128) predicting all 24 hours at once, trained from scratch every day on the same inputs as LEAR-X. Three seeds averaged.

torch_warm.name: PyTorch, warm start
torch_warm.what: A network plus a straight linear path, kept from one day to the next and only updated with the new day instead of retrained.

torch_dist.name: PyTorch, distribution
torch_dist.what: The warm-start network, but it forecasts a Johnson SU distribution for each hour instead of one number. Its median is used here.

chronos2.name: Chronos-2
chronos2.what: Amazon's pretrained time series model, used as it is with no training. It sees twelve weeks of hourly prices, and for tomorrow the weather forecasts, holidays, weekday and gas price.
chronos2.note: Released in October 2025, so its training data may overlap the first weeks here. The days after it are the clean test.

tabpfn.name: TabPFN
tabpfn.what: A pretrained model for tables. Each day it gets the last year as rows (hour, prices 1, 2, 3 and 7 days before, neighbour prices, weather, gas) and predicts tomorrow's rows without training.

chronos2_prices_only.name: Chronos-2, prices only
chronos2_prices_only.what: Chronos-2 on the price series alone, to see how much the weather and gas inputs add. Not a candidate.
